role: THE single authoritative statement of what prevents the Safety InSite v1 candidate from reaching each of three distinct release thresholds. Supersedes BETA-BLOCKERS.json as the release authority; that file remains as the historical §263-§285 record.

thresholds.A: CONTROLLED PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENT — the candidate running in a production environment, no users.
thresholds.B: INTERNAL / OWNER PRODUCTION USE — owner-controlled accounts entering real data.
thresholds.C: EXTERNAL CONTROLLED BETA — named external inspectors entering real workplace data.

entries.description: Liability allocation, caps and exclusions are DELIBERATELY UNDRAFTED in the Terms.

entries.remediation: Counsel drafts liability allocation. A disclaimer does NOT eliminate liability; enforceability of any limitation depends on jurisdiction, conspicuousness, unconscionability and whether the loss is personal injury.
entries.retestRequirement: Counsel-approved clause present and linked from the accepted agreement.

entries.retestRequirement: Both routes reachable, versioned, and linked from signup.

entries.description: The generated report does not overstate what it knows, and its zero-finding language is bounded and falsified.

entries.retestRequirement: validate:286-reports-and-severity Z7/Z8.

entries.description: Public claim-bearing surfaces (/about, /hazlenz, /pricing, marketing copy) have never been audited against the product's own claims guardrails or against FTC substantiation expectations.
entries.currentState: FTC 'Operation AI Comply' remains active into 2026. The closest precedent is FTC v. Evolv Technologies (Nov 2024, settled Dec 2024): an AI DETECTION product barred from unsubstantiated detection claims after failures to detect. HazLenz is a hazard-detection-adjacent claim surface.
entries.evidence: project-docs/legal/CLAIMS-GUARDRAILS.md exists but is not enforced against live copy; ftc.gov Evolv action
entries.remediation: Audit every live claim. Never claim HazLenz detects all hazards, guarantees compliance, or replaces inspection. Substantiate any accuracy/performance claim or remove it.
entries.retestRequirement: A claim-by-claim audit of the four public surfaces against CLAIMS-GUARDRAILS.md.

entries.description: Workplace photographs may contain identifiable individuals; the product has no stated position on that and the Privacy Notice is unapproved.
entries.currentState: Field capture and inspection photos are stored as first-class evidence. No in-product guidance, no consent posture, no retention statement for images of people.
entries.remediation: Counsel-reviewed statement in the Privacy Notice plus in-product guidance on photographing people. State-law exposure varies; this is a risk-management and contractual matter, not a single federal requirement.
entries.retestRequirement: Privacy Notice section approved and a product guidance surface.

entries.description: No self-serve account or data deletion exists. The user entity has deletedAt but no route sets it.
entries.currentState: No DELETE endpoint under users or auth.
entries.evidence: backend/src/users/ (no controller with a Delete route)
entries.remediation: For a named, invitation-only beta a documented MANUAL deletion procedure with a stated turnaround is a defensible position. Self-serve deletion is a v1.1/v2 item. If the beta ever opens beyond named participants, revisit against CCPA/CPRA applicability thresholds.
entries.retestRequirement: A written deletion procedure, and one rehearsed deletion on a disposable database.

entries.description: Authentication and authorization architecture verified: 15-minute access tokens, refresh tokens, production refuses to start without JWT_SECRET, global and per-route throttling, server-owned authority on entitlement and lifecycle state.

entries.remediation: None.
entries.retestRequirement: validate:287-action-lifecycle W-series.

entries.description: Access and refresh tokens are held in localStorage rather than httpOnly cookies.
entries.currentState: Standard SPA trade-off; exposes tokens to any successful XSS. Mitigation today is that no XSS is known and the token life is 15 minutes.
entries.remediation: Accept for controlled beta with a short token life, or move to httpOnly cookies with CSRF protection in v1.1. Record the decision.
entries.retestRequirement: If changed: a full auth regression plus CSRF coverage.

entries.description: No production security review, dependency-vulnerability gate, or penetration test has been performed.
entries.currentState: No automated advisory scan in the release path.
entries.evidence: no security gate in the repository's gate set
entries.remediation: A dependency advisory scan in the release path, and a scoped review of the authenticated API surface before external users. Do not test against production.
entries.retestRequirement: A clean advisory scan and a recorded review.

entries.description: Audit-trail completeness now has a stated failure mode: a failed audit write no longer fails the request and is emitted as action.audit_write_failed (severity error).
entries.currentState: Forced-failure regression proves the customer sees success, the state commits, and the missing row is emitted with actor and transition.
entries.remediation: The emitted event is a fallback record, not an audit trail. If audit completeness is a compliance commitment, a durable queue is required.
entries.retestRequirement: validate:287-action-lifecycle A-series.

entries.description: Cross-account isolation verified on inspections, reports, actions, tasks and calendar, including the §287 edit route.

entries.description: The outcome-intelligence recurrence check counts across EVERY tenant and would auto-escalate one customer's action on another customer's history.
entries.currentState: DISABLED and BLOCKED FROM ACTIVATION by product-owner decision. The outcomes table has no migration; to_regclass('public.outcomes') is NULL and zero migrations reference it.
entries.remediation: Before any activation: scope recurrence to tenant/workspace, prove same-tenant history CAN influence and other-tenant history CANNOT, prove no identifier leakage, no cross-tenant escalation, add query scoping and indexes, and regress with two or more workspaces.
entries.retestRequirement: A two-workspace regression proving both directions.

entries.description: Organization/multi-user workspace paths are only partially exercised; most evidence is from single-user personal accounts.

entries.evidence: backend corrective-actions and tasks services; no multi-member workspace fixture
entries.remediation: A two-member organization fixture exercising owner, assignee, manager and non-member.
entries.retestRequirement: A role-matrix regression on a populated organization.

entries.description: Report and artifact access is an authenticated streaming GET; there are no signed URLs to leak or expire.
entries.currentState: Guarded by JwtGuard + ownership scope; nosniff and sandbox CSP headers on the PDF response.
entries.remediation: None. This is a stronger model than signed URLs and should be preserved.
entries.retestRequirement: Report download authorization tests.

entries.description: OFFLINE CONFLICT RESOLUTION does not exist, and OFFLINE HAZLENZ INTELLIGENCE does not exist.

entries.description: D-053 residual: corrective-action EDIT and CLOSE carry no idempotency key.
entries.currentState: CREATE was repaired at §287 (clientRequestId + partial unique index) and all three duplicate modes are proven. EDIT and CLOSE are idempotent in EFFECT because they set a target state rather than appending, and the client sends them with retries:0, so nothing is silently re-sent.
entries.remediation: Extend the clientRequestId pattern to the two mutation routes, OR accept last-write-wins and state it. This is a PRECONDITION for any future offline outbox, not a live defect: no duplicate has been produced by either route.
entries.retestRequirement: A duplicate-submission measurement on both routes.

entries.retestRequirement: A fresh-database migration run confirming the head and the three added columns.

entries.description: Structured operational events are emitted to stdout/stderr with redaction, but there is no aggregation, alerting, error tracking or incident runbook.
entries.currentState: No APM or error-tracking dependency in either package. A failure in production would be discovered by a person looking.
entries.remediation: Aggregate the operational event stream, alert on the error-severity events that already exist (report.generation_failed, action.audit_write_failed, schema.readiness_failed, migration.failed), and write a minimal incident runbook with an owner and a contact path.
entries.retestRequirement: One alert fired end to end from a deliberately induced error-severity event.

entries.description: Dependency licensing surveyed across both packages: overwhelmingly MIT/ISC/Apache-2.0/BSD. No infecting copyleft in the application graph.
entries.currentState: Frontend ~420 packages, backend ~480. The only notable items are LGPL-3.0-or-later on sharp's libvips binaries (dynamically linked, redistributed unmodified) and CC-BY-4.0 on caniuse-lite (build-time data).
entries.remediation: Record an attribution/notice file covering LGPL and CC-BY components before external distribution. No license here prevents commercial use.
entries.retestRequirement: Re-run the license survey when dependencies change.

entries.description: Federal regulatory text (29 CFR OSHA, 30 CFR MSHA) is reproduced from eCFR sources.
entries.currentState: Federal regulations are government edicts and are not subject to copyright. Reproduction and redistribution are unproblematic.
entries.remediation: None. Keep the eCFR provenance records with the shipped content.
entries.retestRequirement: Existing source-integrity verifiers.

entries.description: Privately authored consensus standards (ANSI, ASTM, NFPA, ANSI/ASSP) are referenced by NAME AND TOPICAL SCOPE ONLY. No standard text is reproduced anywhere in the shipped product.
entries.currentState: Inspected: entries carry authorityName, a one-line in-house shortUse, an applicability guardrail and reasoning keywords. Titles and citations plus original in-house summaries.
entries.remediation: This is the correct posture and must be PRESERVED as a hard rule. ASTM v. Public.Resource.Org (D.C. Cir. 2023) held that NON-COMMERCIAL posting of incorporated-by-reference standards is fair use; the standards remain copyrighted and that holding does not extend to a COMMERCIAL product redistributing the text. Incorporation by reference does not make private standard text freely redistributable here.
entries.retestRequirement: A content gate asserting no private standard text is ever ingested into shipped content.

entries.description: Fonts, icons and images: the only icon dependency is lucide-react (ISC). No licensed font or stock imagery is bundled.
entries.currentState: No @font-face or Google Fonts import in the shipped layout or stylesheet.
entries.remediation: None. Preserve when brand assets are added.
entries.retestRequirement: Re-check when assets change.

entries.description: SAFETY INSITE is treated as NOT FORMALLY CLEARED. No trademark search, clearance opinion or application is recorded.
entries.currentState: 'InSite' is a common construction/safety-software formative, which raises the likelihood of conflicting commercial use.
entries.evidence: no clearance record in the repository
entries.remediation: Commission a clearance search before external commercialization. A controlled, invitation-only beta under a name later found to conflict is a recoverable but real rebranding cost. Do not rename in this section.
entries.retestRequirement: A recorded clearance opinion.

entries.description: HazLenz has had no conflict or provenance check.
entries.currentState: A coined term, so a priori lower conflict risk than SAFETY INSITE, but unverified.
entries.remediation: Include in the same clearance search as TM-1.
entries.retestRequirement: A recorded clearance opinion.

entries.description: If an operator relies on Safety InSite output as their statutory examination record, the product's retention and export properties become regulatorily significant.
entries.currentState: MSHA 30 CFR 56.18002 requires a competent person designated by the operator to examine each working place each shift, a record made before the end of that shift, and RETENTION FOR ONE YEAR available to the Secretary. OSHA imposes separate recordkeeping duties under 29 CFR 1904. The product neither performs the examination nor guarantees the record.
entries.evidence: ecfr.gov 30 CFR 56.18002; the product has no retention guarantee
entries.remediation: State plainly, in Terms and in product copy, that Safety InSite does not perform the statutory examination and does not itself satisfy any recordkeeping obligation, and that the operator remains responsible for making and retaining required records. Pair with ST-3 to give customers a dependable export.
entries.retestRequirement: A copy audit plus a demonstrated export of a full inspection record.

entries.description: Report revision retention is implemented and proven: every issued revision is retained, byte-identical, downloadable, and marked superseded with a link to its successor.
entries.currentState: Customer-reachable since §286. A superseded artifact is never rewritten.
entries.remediation: None.
entries.retestRequirement: validate:286-reports-and-severity R/C series.

entries.description: The only outbound email is password reset, via Resend, and production refuses to run without PASSWORD_RESET_PROVIDER=resend. All other notifications are in-app database rows with no delivery.

entries.remediation: Decide whether the beta needs any outbound notification beyond password reset. If not, ensure no surface implies a user will be emailed when work is assigned to them.
entries.retestRequirement: A copy audit of anything implying notification delivery.

entries.description: project-docs/preservation/v1-beta/ does not exist. There is no build-and-restore guide and no machine-readable release manifest.
entries.currentState: The inputs exist: release-identity.ts already derives releaseVersion, gitSha, buildTimestamp, backend/frontend versions and schemaCompatibilityVersion (now correct after DB-2).
entries.remediation: Create the directory, the guide, and a manifest containing productVersion, gitSha, sourceDigest, hazlenzIdentity, frontendVersion, backendVersion, schemaCompatibilityVersion, migrationHead, nodeVersion, npmVersion, databaseVersion, buildTimestamp, knownLimitations, canonicalDocs and validationEvidence.
entries.retestRequirement: A rebuild from the guide reproducing the recorded identities.

entries.description: The historical digest 3c2c5974... is MISATTRIBUTED and must not be used as a current integrity assertion.
entries.currentState: Exhaustively searched at §283: absent from the working tree, all 17,102 git objects, and all four stashes; no derivation from the frozen baseline reproduces it.
entries.remediation: Use instead: commit 709ee151..., the per-document digests in verification/current/LOCAL-PRODUCT-BASELINE.json, and the §274 successor identity 8c163b31..., which verify:274-successor-identity recomputes from live sources.
entries.retestRequirement: verify:274-successor-identity.

entries.description: No release runbook and no tested rollback procedure exist for either the frontend or the backend.
entries.currentState: Migrations are forward-only in practice; the §287 migration has a working down() but a general rollback position is undefined.
entries.remediation: Write the release runbook (order of operations, backup point, migration step, verification step) and define rollback for each half, including what happens to a migration that has already run.
entries.retestRequirement: A rehearsed rollback on a disposable target.

entries.description: No production acceptance procedure is defined: after deploying, nothing states what must be true before a human is allowed to use the system.
entries.currentState: All acceptance to date is local-stack acceptance against a disposable database.
entries.remediation: Define a short post-deploy acceptance: health and readiness, version/SHA match, one real inspection to a generated report, storage round-trip, entitlement boundary, and the operational event stream visible.
entries.retestRequirement: The acceptance executed against the controlled production environment and recorded.
